 Appellate Side

(Item No. 12)
(AB)
 W.P.A. 16832 of 2024  +
 CAN 1 of 2024  +
 CAN 2 of 2024  Alamgir Khan  VS  The Union of India & Ors.
 Mr. Kushal Chatterjee  Mr. Iftekar Munshi
..... for the petitioner  Mr. Surajit Chakraborty
..... for GAIL

Sk. Md. Galib  Mr. Abu Siddique Mallik  ..... for respondent Nos. 11 & 12 Ms. Ajeya Mitra Mr. K. K. Chakraborti Ms. Srijani Das ..... for the intervenor Mr. Soumitra Bandyopadhyay Ms. Suchana Banerjee ..... for the State In Re: CAN 1 of 2024 With CAN 2 of 2024 Affidavit of service filed in Court today is taken on record.
Ms. Ajeya Mitra, learned counsel appearing for the applicants praying for intervention in the main writ petition.

On a reading of both these applications and from the reliefs claimed therein, it appears to this Court that, her clients claim compensation for utilization of land on which her clients claim rights and interest, there is no prayer for intervention or for being added as parties to this writ petition.
The applications are vehemently opposed by the writ petitioner and also opposed by respondent Nos. 11 and 12 and the State.
In course of the submissions, Ms. Mitra upon obtaining instructions from her clients submits that,
her clients shall withdraw these two applications and shall file a composite application with proper reliefs.

sentences.text: In view of the above, these two applications, CAN 1 of 2024 and CAN 2 of 2024 stand dismissed as withdrawn with leave to file a composite application by the clients of Ms. Ajeya Mitra, learned counsel on the self-same cause of action with appropriate reliefs.
In the event such applications are filed, the same shall be served upon the writ petitioner and all other respondents in the writ petition.
Affidavit of service shall be filed accordingly when the matter shall be taken up next.
In Re: W.P.A. 16832 of 2024 The last order dated September 17, 2024 speaks for itself in detail.

Mr. Kushal Chatterjee, learned counsel appearing for the alleged Mutawalli of Edbar Ali Khan Waqf Estate (for short, Waqf) submits that, the respondent No. 13 for the purpose of laying out Gas Lines for the public purpose are in the process of utilizing a portion of the Waqf land without any prior consultation with the Waqf Board which is a mandatory requirement under Section 51 of the Waqf Act, 1995 (for short, Waqf Act).
Mr. Chatterjee, learned counsel for the petitioner prays for an interim order, as prayed for in the writ petition.

Pursuant to the direction made by this Court on September 17, 2024 Mr. Soumitra Bandyopadhyay,
learned State counsel submits a bunch of documents appended to a report dated July 25, 2024 submitted by respondent No. 3, the same is taken on record.

From the said report it appears that, on September 24, 2021 a Gazette notification was published under Sub-Section (1) of Section 3 of the Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962.

entities.text: Petroleum and Minerals Pipelines (Acquisition of Right of User in Land) Act, 1962
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further Gazette notification was published under Sub-Section 1 to Section 6 of the 1962 Act on January 20, 2022.
The requiring and acquiring bodies have proceeded to acquire the land on the basis of the available land record.

The factum of acquisition was within the knowledge of the petitioner and still the petitioner did not raise or submit any objection objecting to such acquisition process before the appropriate authority.
The laying down of pipeline has achieved a substantial progress and at this juncture the petitioner has filed this writ petition.
Since the laying down of Gas Pipeline is for public purpose for the utility of the public at large the same shall not be interfered with at this juncture.
The possession of the relevant land was taken over by the acquiring body on September 13, 2024 as would be evident from the said bunch of documents.
The GAIL in turn has taken over possession of the subject land for laying down the pipeline.

Sk. Md. Galib, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos. 11 and 12, the Waqf Board submits that, challenging the appointment of the petitioner as Mutawalli a substantive proceeding is pending before the Waqf Tribunal.
He further submits that by virtue of a Civil Court decree the relevant property has been declared as a Waqf property.
Whether any consultation has taken place in terms of Section 51 of the Waqf Act, he submits that he shall disclose the relevant documents through an affidavit.

Mr. Surajit Chakraborty, learned counsel appearing for respondent No. 13 (GAIL) submits since the work is under taken for public purpose and has progressed substantially, no interim order can be passed at this stage.

sentences.text: Per contra, relying upon Section 6 (1) Gazette notification under the said 1962 Act learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the plot Nos. 142, 143, 93 and 177 though are part of the Waqf property but they are not mentioned in the said 6(1) Gazette notification.
However, pipelines are laying down through those plots.

Learned State counsel Mr. Bandyopadhyay has denied and disputed the said submission made on behalf of the petitioner and referring to the report filed today, he submits that through the said plots no alignment of Gas Pipe Line was laid down, however those plots are recorded neither in the name of the petitioner nor in the name of the Waqf.
GAIL has also not laid down any pipelines through these four number of plots.

After considering the rival contentions of the parties and upon perusal of the materials on record, it appears to this Court that, the two Gazette notifications under Sections 3(1) and 6(1) of the 1962 Act are available which were published in the year 2021 and 2022 respectively.
The moment the Gazette notification was published under Section 3(1) of the 1962 Act, it is deemed, by fiction of law, that the said notification is within the knowledge of the petitioner.
Therefore, the petitioner chose not to raise any objection with the acquisition process even after the said Gazette notification was caused under Section 3(1) of the 1962 Act.
Whether the pipeline has been laying down through the said four numbers of plots being L.R. Nos. 177, 142, 143 and 93 can only be ascertained after affidavits are filed by the respondents.
The laying down of Gas Pipeline is for the public purpose to serve public utility at large at the locale.
Prima facie, it appears from record that the authorities have complied with the steps under Section 3(1) and 6(1) of the said Act of 1962 at least by publishing the Gazette notifications.
The question of appointment of the petitioner as Mutawalli is pending adjudication before the jurisdictional Waqf Tribunal.
So long the same is finally disposed of, this Court shall not express any opinion on that issue.

Applying the legal principles for granting an interim order, this Court is of the firm view that, for the purpose of acquisition of a land the requiring or acquiring body shall primarily proceed on the basis of the land records available with the appropriate State authority.
As submitted on behalf of the respondents that the land records on the basis where of the acquisition proceeding was initiated, the land was not found to be recorded in the name of the Waqf.
In addition the due notifications, as narrated above, have already been published in the official Gazettes.
Despite knowledge and/or deemed knowledge the petitioner chose not to raise any objection at the appropriate stage with regard to the acquisition process.
Therefore, there is no prima facie case made out for granting an order of injunction to stall the laying down of Gas Pipeline for the public interest at large.
The petitioner in the above facts and circumstance has also failed to establish the balance of convenience and/or inconvenience in favour of passing an interim order.
In view of the above discussions and reasons, there shall be no interim order.

sentences.text: Affidavits are called for.

Respondents shall file their affidavits-in- opposition on or before November 20, 2024. Affidavit- in-reply, if any, thereto shall be filed by November 29, 2024.
The writ petition shall appear under the heading "Hearing (Land Matter)" in the monthly list of December 2024.
However, the steps taken and shall be taken arising out of the acquisition of the subject land shall abide by the result of this writ petition.

It is also made clear that, depending upon the facts and situation, the question of compensation, if any, payable to the land owners in accordance with law, may be taken note of at the appropriate stage.

(Aniruddha Roy, J.)
